prompt: Use showntell to give a newcomer a tour of this repository: what showntell does, how a walkthrough travels from the agent's Markdown to the browser, and where the speech comes from. Read the code first and show real code from disk. About three minutes.
Use showntell to review commit 8db41e4 in this repo for another developer: what problem it fixes in the player, how the fix works, and anything to watch. Show the real diff from git.
Use showntell to explain the TLS 1.3 handshake: what each message does, why it needs only one round trip, and where the keys come from. Use a sequence diagram.
Use showntell to explain scaled dot-product attention in transformers, including why the scores are divided by the square root of the key dimension. Use formulas and a tiny worked example.
Use showntell, in the portrait frame for phones, to explain git rebase versus merge with diagrams of the commit graph. Keep it under two minutes.
